prompt: I do not know which workflow mode I need. Explain the current recovery model.
required: answers through the least expensive read-only path
does not require a skill name or CLI command
reports trustworthy gaps separately
forbidden: asks the user to choose a workflow command
starts reconstruction merely because knowledge is incomplete
rewrites knowledge while explaining

prompt: Current knowledge seems incomplete. What can you tell me and what would it take to establish a baseline?
required: provides the useful current answer first
explains the gap, cost, and output of reconstruction
gives a recommendation
asks one focused confirmation before starting
forbidden: silently starts a whole-project reconstruction
requires the user to name repositories already in the registry
presents search rank as coverage

prompt: Shape a cross-Area account-security direction whose recovery, session, and ownership choices depend on each other.
required: uses one canonical bundle with a low-resolution map and question issues
separates precise frontier questions from still-unphraseable fog and out-of-scope work
finds discoverable facts before asking
asks one highest-leverage question with a recommendation
records the full answer in its issue before asking the next question
does not edit product source
forbidden: creates a separate direction or strategy source
sends a questionnaire
writes an implementation plan while destination choices remain unresolved

prompt: The direction is now approved and the next bounded change is clear.
required: records approval and deferred questions
reads every resolved issue and synthesizes the same bundle through specify-project-change
converts the clear route into stable observable acceptance IDs before delivery issues
forbidden: copies the direction into a second spec
promotes proposals as current truth
loses rejected or superseded decisions

prompt: We changed one acceptance rule during an active implementation session; preserve it before the session compacts.
required: updates the owning change or claimed issue instead of creating an inbox record
records the semantic change and rationale before refreshing the checkpoint
refreshes the checkpoint last with current state, last action, next action, blockers, and actor
still requires complete record reads after resume
forbidden: copies active progress into changes/inbox
treats the checkpoint as a replacement for the specification
relies on conversation memory after compaction

prompt: While implementing an active issue, you discover an undocumented invariant, a misleading test fixture, and a possible product implication. Preserve whatever a fresh session will need.
required: uses consequence of information loss rather than a closed finding taxonomy
records each consequential observation with evidence or missing evidence, implication, scope, and disposition in the owning discovery ledger
keeps uncertain observations uncertain and preserves later invalidation as lineage
updates semantic state before refreshing the checkpoint last
forbidden: stores full discoveries only in checkpoint prose
creates an inbox capture for material already owned by the active issue
turns routine command history into a discovery log

prompt: I opened a clean agent session in this repository. Resume the active work; I do not know its workflow ID.
required: runs work context in resume mode without requiring an ID
auto-selects only one bound active record and asks the maintainer when several exist
reads every required file and discovery entry completely
verifies the exact claim and code roots before acting
forbidden: asks the user for a workflow ID
selects work from recency, branch name, or a sibling checkout
resumes from checkpoint prose without reading its semantic owner

prompt: A lightweight investigation found a reusable constraint, but no active change or knowledge concept owns it yet.
required: creates one pending non-authoritative capture
retains exact source identity and evidence
leaves it pending while authority or destination is missing
creates real destinations before resolving it as routed or discards it with a reason
forbidden: presents the capture as current truth
leaves a routed copy in changes/inbox
creates a capture when an active owner already exists

prompt: Implement ISSUE-004 after a new session started in a linked worktree.
required: runs work status and stage-specific context
reads the complete parent, issue, blockers, and referenced artifacts
records current hash receipts before claiming
claims the issue from the exact bound worktree before source work
forbidden: infers a sibling checkout from repository or branch name
reads only headings or map summaries
creates a second issue tracker in the leaf

prompt: Verify and close a multi-file change bundle after implementation.
required: inventories every bundle file recursively
re-reads changed-after-review files
maps every stable acceptance ID to evidence
checks all issues, blockers, claims, revisions, and knowledge promotion
forbidden: treats a generated inventory as semantic proof
ignores an artifact or issue because its title seems irrelevant
closes with an unresolved map or dirty checkout

prompt: During shaping, the team uses account, identity, profile, and player interchangeably.
required: records term candidates, definitions, contextual boundaries, aliases, and names to avoid
checks current Area terminology
keeps unresolved terms in the active spec
promotes only explicitly accepted vocabulary
forbidden: creates a flattened global glossary by default
silently chooses the most frequent term
changes current knowledge during unresolved discussion

prompt: Several implementation details changed, and the team repeatedly rejected resurrection without a special item.
required: creates standalone decisions only for hard-to-reverse, surprising, or real-tradeoff choices
keeps routine choices in the owning concept, ledger, or Area evolution
keeps rejected proposals case-only
asks whether the repeated boundary is an accepted durable non-goal
forbidden: creates one decision record per implementation detail
promotes rejection through repetition
deletes the rejected proposal history

prompt: Research the current passkey recovery standards for a pending architecture decision.
required: bounds the decision and freshness scope
prefers and directly reads primary sources
records a claim-to-source matrix, conflicts, applicability, and limits
stores the synthesis in the owning record or a pending non-authoritative capture
requires normal authority before project conclusions become current knowledge
forbidden: treats search snippets as evidence
lets an external standard authorize project intent
silently curates the agent summary

prompt: Resume processing a large raw dump.
required: shows generation, accounting counts, active themes, blockers, decisions, next batch, and completion condition
derives the frontier from inventory and cases
continues bounded batches
forbidden: guesses unseen file contents from names
stores a competing manual ledger
claims completion from QMD retrieval

prompt: Resume a multi-repository baseline after compaction.
required: restores the case and exact bindings
shows outstanding files, communities, surfaces, optional inputs, reconciliation, claims, and decisions
names the highest-leverage next action
keeps complete CLI ledgers authoritative for accounting
forbidden: uses a percentage to hide pending items
mistakes one completed dossier for whole-project completion
reconstructs state from chat memory

prompt: Start a baseline reconstruction. The frozen raw snapshot contains several large historical and product-idea themes.
required: inventories and maps raw only far enough to recommend all, selected themes, or exclusion
asks the maintainer one project-language scope question
records the exact human actor, time, paths, and rationale through reconstruction raw-scope
starts reconstruction-owned intake only after approval with the parent reconstruction binding
forbidden: silently includes all raw because files exist
requires the maintainer to know raw pathspec syntax
invents a human approval actor
starts or reuses an unbound intake case before the scope decision

prompt: I opened a clean session in the knowledge repository. Continue the active reconstruction; I do not know its ID.
required: runs reconstruction context in JSON mode without requiring an ID
auto-selects only one active reconstruction and asks by human outcome when several exist
reads the complete parent case, every repository dossier, and local binding
recovers the complete coverage frontier including items absent from prose
treats a stale checkpoint as a hint and rebuilds state before refreshing it
forbidden: selects a case by recency or directory order
reads only dossier headings or coverage summaries
copies operational discoveries into curated knowledge
trusts checkpoint prose after its basis becomes stale

prompt: During reconstruction we found a repository-local invariant and a cross-repository product implication. Preserve them before compaction.
required: records the local invariant in its repository dossier discovery ledger
records the cross-repository implication in the parent case discovery ledger
preserves observation, evidence boundary, implication, scope, and disposition
updates semantic records before refreshing the reconstruction checkpoint last
forbidden: stores both discoveries only in checkpoint prose
promotes either discovery as truth without adjudication
uses curated knowledge as a reconstruction scratchpad

prompt: Continue the active raw-intake batch in this clean session; I do not remember the case ID.
required: runs intake case context in JSON mode without requiring an ID
reads the complete case and recovers every pending or blocked frozen source
preserves consequential discoveries in the case rather than checkpoint-only prose
asks by human batch title when several cases are active
forbidden: guesses the case from timestamps
uses QMD snippets as complete source review
treats the intake case or its discoveries as curated truth

prompt: Verify a stable product capability before publication.
required: runs structural validation separately
pins the candidate content hash
reviews authority and truth independently from reader communication
binds both passed axes to the same unchanged content hash
reruns both passes after a material edit
forbidden: lets good prose compensate for unsupported facts
lets strong evidence compensate for an unusable explanation
uses one review verdict as proof of the other axis
